speaker: Algenib
style: Say warmly with a gravelly voice, like an old park ranger teaching a new lookout.
lines: Tap the map to put up a smoke. Both towers swing their sights onto it.
Tower C draws a circle with the law of cosines. The fire sits on it.
These sights never cross. Tap a smoke off the line between the towers.
The sights line up. No triangle, so no fix. Ask a tower off this line.
Tap Smoke 1 to start. Then drag each tower's sight handle onto the smoke.
Drag each round sight handle onto the smoke. Or Tab to a handle and turn it with the arrow keys.
Type the three angles inside the triangle. They add to one hundred eighty degrees.
Use the law of sines. Type the distance from tower A to the fire, then press Check.
Now tower C. Use the law of cosines to type the distance from C, then press Check.
Press Dispatch crew to send the truck.
That checks out.
This guided step checks out.
Not yet. Look at the step the note points to, then fix that box.
Crew on scene.
A crew radioed one distance. Tap how many spots fit, then tap each spot on the map.
Tap each spot where the circle meets the forward sight. Or move the map crosshair and press Enter.
Press No spot to confirm that the circle never reaches the sight.
Two spots fit the same numbers. That is the ambiguous case.
Two crews walked the fire's edge from one corner. Type the area, then press Check.
The worked solution is shown. Use it to finish this guided example.
Angle A is the gap between A's azimuth to B, seventy degrees, and A's azimuth to the smoke.

Tap another clearing, or press Show the law of sines to work this triangle.
Crew en route. Choose another smoke or mode to cancel the drive.
Crew on scene. Pick another smoke to survey a different triangle.
Look where the circle crosses the sight, then choose 0 spots, 1 spot, or 2 spots again.
Read the SSA work, then choose another call to compare how many locations fit.
Choose another burn to compare an acute, obtuse, and right included angle.
Tap the map to place a smoke. Tower C can then check its distance.
Saved check marks cleared. Choose a smoke to survey it.
Guided example shown. Press Check area to compare with the shaded survey.
Values changed. Press Check area to check this guided example again.
Worked example shown. Press Check to continue this guided survey.
Type each angle as a whole number of degrees. Fix the box, then press Check.
Angle A: compare the two azimuths leaving A. Fix the box, then press Check.
Angle B: use the direction from B back to A, 250°. Fix the box, then press Check.
Angle F should make the three angles add to 180. Fix the box, then press Check.
Type a number of miles. Fix the box, then press Check.
AF: pair each side with the sine of its opposite angle. Fix the box, then press Check.
CF: use the included angle CAF, between AC and AF. Fix the box, then press Check.
Type an area in square miles. Fix the boxes, then press Check area.
Type acres as a whole number. Fix the boxes, then press Check area.
Square miles: use half the product of the sides and the sine of the included angle. Fix the boxes, then press Check area.
Acres: multiply the unrounded square miles by 640. Fix the boxes, then press Check area.
